title: VOZ PASIVA (BÁSICA)
subtitle: The passive · present and past simple

map.center: Usamos la VOZ PASIVA cuando lo importante es la acción o lo que le pasa a algo, no quién lo hace.

nodes.title: ¿Qué es?
items: El objeto pasa a ser el sujeto.

error.title: Error común
bad: Don Quixote was wrote by Cervantes.
good: Don Quixote was written by Cervantes.

mini.es: Completa con la pasiva: is / are / was / were + participio.

explain.es: En la voz activa el sujeto hace la acción: Leo paints the wall. En la voz pasiva el sujeto recibe la acción: The wall is painted. La usamos cuando lo importante es la acción o el objeto, no quién lo hace (porque no lo sabemos, no importa o es obvio). En español solemos decirlo con «se» (se habla inglés, se construyó en 1890), con ser + participio (fue construido) o con un «ellos» impersonal (me robaron la bici).
explain.en: In the passive, the subject receives the action. We use it when the action or the object is more important than who does it.

explain.title: 1 · De activa a pasiva
explain.es: Para pasar una frase a pasiva: 1) el objeto de la activa pasa a ser el sujeto; 2) ponemos be en el mismo tiempo que el verbo activo; 3) añadimos el participio del verbo principal; 4) si queremos decir quién lo hizo, usamos by.
explain.en: Active object → passive subject. Then be (same tense) + past participle (+ by + agent).

examples.en: Millions of people watch the final. → The final is watched by millions of people.
examples.es: Millones de personas ven la final. → La final la ven millones de personas.

examples.en: Someone stole my bike. → My bike was stolen.
examples.es: Alguien me robó la bici. → Me robaron la bici.

examples.en: They sell tickets online. → Tickets are sold online.
examples.es: Venden las entradas por internet. → Las entradas se venden por internet.

explain.title: 2 · Present simple passive
explain.es: am / is / are + participio. Sirve para hechos generales, procesos y cosas que pasan normalmente. Concordancia: is con singular o incontable, are con plural. Muy típico con made, spoken, sold, used, grown, played.
explain.en: am / is / are + past participle for facts, processes and routines.

examples.es: La mayoría de los móviles se fabrican en Asia.

explain.title: 3 · Past simple passive
explain.es: was / were + participio. Sirve para hechos del pasado: historia, noticias, inventos, construcciones, descubrimientos, delitos… was con singular, were con plural.
explain.en: was / were + past participle for past events, history and news.

examples.en: The Alhambra was built in the 13th and 14th centuries.
examples.es: La Alhambra se construyó en los siglos XIII y XIV.

examples.en: Penicillin was discovered by Alexander Fleming in 1928.
examples.es: La penicilina fue descubierta por Alexander Fleming en 1928.

examples.en: Two players were injured during the match.
examples.es: Dos jugadores resultaron heridos durante el partido.

explain.title: Todo junto
head: Tiempo · Tense
✅ Afirmativa
⛔ Negativa
❓ Pregunta
Traducción · Spanish
explain.note: Solo cambia be (is / are / was / were). El participio no cambia nunca: made, built, written…
explain.note_en: Only be changes. The past participle never changes.

explain.title: 4 · Negativas y preguntas
explain.es: Como en cualquier frase con be: negativa con not (isn't, aren't, wasn't, weren't) y pregunta poniendo be delante del sujeto. ¡Sin do / does / did! Did the window broken? → Was the window broken?
explain.en: Negative: be + not. Question: be before the subject. No do / does / did.

examples.es: El desayuno no está incluido en el precio.
¿Te invitaron a la boda de Lucía?
¿Cuándo se construyó la Torre Eiffel? — En 1889.

explain.title: 5 · BY + agente
explain.es: Si queremos decir quién hace la acción, usamos by (= por): written by Shakespeare. Pero solo lo ponemos cuando es información importante o nueva. No ponemos by someone, by people, by them ni agentes obvios: The thief was arrested (¡ya sabemos que fue la policía!).
explain.en: Use by + agent only when it's important or new information. Don't say by someone / by people.

examples.es: El Guernica fue pintado por Picasso.

examples.en: This song was written by a 15-year-old girl!
examples.es: ¡Esta canción la escribió una chica de 15 años!

examples.en: My wallet was stolen on the metro. (no sabemos quién)
examples.es: Me robaron la cartera en el metro.

explain.title: ¿ACTIVA o PASIVA?
explain.es: Elige la pasiva cuando el protagonista es la cosa o la acción. Elige la activa cuando lo importante es la persona que lo hace.
explain.en: Passive: the thing or the action matters. Active: the person who does it matters.

explain.title: Participios que vas a necesitar
head: Verbo · Verb
Participio
Ejemplo · Example
rows: It was found in a cave.
Paella is eaten all over Spain.
The photo was taken in Rome.
explain.note: Regulares: -ed (used, invented, cleaned). Ojo: el participio es la 3.ª columna de los irregulares, no la 2.ª: was wrote → was written.
explain.note_en: Use the 3rd column (past participle), not the past simple.

explain.title: Del español al inglés
head: Español
Inglés · English
explain.note: Truco: cuando en español dices «se + verbo» o «me / nos + verbo en plural» sin decir quién (me robaron, nos invitaron), en inglés suele ir pasiva. ¡Nunca traduzcas ese «se» por itself!
explain.note_en: Spanish «se» or an impersonal «they» → English passive.

explain.title: Pasivas de todos los días
head: Expresión
Significado
Ejemplo · Example
rows: The hotel is located near the beach.
explain.note: ¡Ojo! Nacer en inglés va en pasiva: I was born in Madrid. Nunca I born ni I am born para hablar de tu nacimiento.
explain.note_en: «Nacer» is passive in English: I was born (never «I born»).

items.bad: The book was wrote by Cervantes.
items.why: Pasiva = be + participio (3.ª columna), no pasado.
Calco de «se habla»: necesitas be + participio.

items.bad: These cars is made in Japan.

items.why: La pasiva pregunta con be, no con did.
El agente va con by (no from, no for).

items.bad: My bike was stolen by someone.

items.why: happen, arrive, die… no tienen pasiva (no llevan objeto).
items.why_en: Verbs with no object have no passive.

items.es: Busca el objeto de la frase activa: será el nuevo sujeto.
items.en: The active object becomes the subject.

items.es: Mira el tiempo: presente → am / is / are; pasado → was / were.
items.en: Present → am / is / are. Past → was / were.

items.es: Haz concordar be con el nuevo sujeto (singular / plural).
items.en: Make be agree with the subject.

items.es: Añade el participio (3.ª columna: made, built, written…).
¿Es importante quién lo hizo? Añade by + agente. Si no, ¡no lo pongas!
items.en: Add by + agent only if it matters.

lines.en: This castle was built in the 12th century.
lines.es: Este castillo se construyó en el siglo XII.

lines.en: Wow! Who was it built by?
By a local king. Later, it was used as a prison for many years.
lines.es: Un rey de la zona. Más tarde se usó como cárcel durante muchos años.

lines.en: Some are. That one was painted by Goya, but the others are copies.
lines.es: Algunos sí. Ese lo pintó Goya, pero los demás son copias.

lines.en: Yes, but flash isn't allowed. The paintings are easily damaged.
lines.es: Sí, pero no se permite el flash. Los cuadros se dañan fácilmente.

lines.en: No problem. Thanks for the tour!

explain.title: Truco: ¿hace o recibe?
explain.es: Pregúntate: ¿el sujeto hace la acción o la recibe? The pizza makes… ¿La pizza hace algo? ¡No! La pizza is made. Si el sujeto recibe la acción → be + participio.
explain.en: Does the subject do the action or receive it? If it receives it → be + past participle.

exercises.text_title: From bean to bar: the story of chocolate
text: Chocolate is made from cacao beans. These beans are grown in hot countries near the equator, like Ivory Coast, Ghana and Ecuador. Most of the world's cacao is produced in West Africa.

Long ago, cacao was used by the Olmecs, the Maya and the Aztecs in Mexico and Central America. It wasn't eaten as a sweet: it was drunk as a bitter drink, often with chilli. In the 16th century, cacao was taken to Spain by Spanish explorers, and sugar was added to make it sweeter.

Today, the beans are picked by hand, dried in the sun and sent to factories. There, they are roasted and ground into a paste. Then milk and sugar are added, and the chocolate is poured into moulds. Millions of tonnes of chocolate are eaten every year!

items.q: Cacao beans are grown in cold countries.
items.why: They're grown in hot countries near the equator.

items.q: Most cacao is produced in West Africa.
At first, cacao was eaten as a sweet.
items.why: It was drunk as a bitter drink.

items.q: The beans are picked by machines.
Who was cacao used by long ago?
items.a: It was used by the Olmecs, the Maya and the Aztecs.

items.q: When was cacao taken to Spain?
items.a: It was taken to Spain in the 16th century.

items.q: What is done to the beans in the factories?
items.a: They are roasted and ground into a paste.

items.q: Find four passive verbs in the text.
items.a: Any four: is made, are grown, is produced, was used, was drunk, was taken, was added, are picked, are roasted, is poured, are eaten…

exercises.title: Ahora escribe tú
exercises.es: Escribe frases en pasiva sobre tu mundo.
exercises.en: Write passive sentences about your world.

items.q: Escribe 2 frases sobre tu región o país: … is made / is grown / is spoken…
items.a: Ej.: Olive oil is produced in my region. Spanish and Catalan are spoken in my city.

items.q: Escribe 2 frases sobre un monumento o un invento: … was built / was invented…
items.a: Ej.: The Roman bridge in my town was built 2,000 years ago. The bicycle was invented in the 19th century.

items.q: Escribe una «noticia» de 2 frases con was / were + participio.
items.a: Ej.: A famous painting was stolen from a museum last night. The thieves were seen by a security guard.

items.q: Escribe 2 preguntas para un concurso: When was… invented? Who was… written by?
items.a: Ej.: When was the telephone invented? Who was Don Quixote written by?

checklist.en: I can form the passive: be + past participle.

checklist.es: Uso is / are (presente) y was / were (pasado) según el sujeto.
checklist.en: I use is / are and was / were correctly.

checklist.es: Uso el participio (3.ª columna): written, built, stolen…
checklist.en: I use the past participle, not the past simple.

checklist.es: Uso by solo cuando importa quién lo hace.
checklist.en: I use by only when the agent is important.

checklist.es: Hago preguntas y negativas con be: Was it built…? It isn't made…
checklist.en: I make questions and negatives with be.

checklist.es: Traduzco «se habla», «me robaron»… con la pasiva.
checklist.en: I can translate Spanish «se» sentences into the passive.
